Contributing to sheepdog

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution. This document explains how to report problems and how to propose changes.

Reporting a bug or asking a question

Open an issue at https://github.com/diogoprov/sheepdog/issues. Please include:

  • a minimal reproducible example, ideally made with reprex (the example data in system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog") is usually enough to reproduce a problem without sharing your recordings);
  • the output of sessionInfo() and the version of sheepdog (packageVersion("sheepdog"));
  • for problems with BirdNET outputs, the BirdNET-Analyzer version and model that produced the selection tables.

Proposing a change

Small fixes (typos, documentation) can go straight to a pull request. For larger changes, such as a new sampling design or a new calibration model, please open an issue first so that we can agree on the approach.

  1. Fork the repository and create a branch from main.
  2. Make your change. Document new or changed functions with roxygen2 and run devtools::document(). The documentation also runs the roclet of srr, which tracks the rOpenSci statistical standards, so install srr first (install.packages("srr", repos = "https://ropensci-review-tools.r-universe.dev")).
  3. Add tests with testthat under tests/testthat/. Tests that need Stan, crywolf or other optional packages must be skipped when those packages are missing.
  4. Run devtools::check() and make sure it finishes with no errors or warnings.
  5. Add a bullet to the top of NEWS.md describing the change.
  6. Open a pull request against main. Continuous integration runs R CMD check on Windows, macOS and Linux and reports test coverage.

Tests that fit Stan models

The default test run (devtools::test(), R CMD check) never compiles a Stan model: the code paths of engine = "brms" are tested with a mocked brms::brm(). The tests that fit real Bayesian models are switched on by an environment variable:

Sys.setenv(SHEEPDOG_TEST_BRMS = "true")
devtools::test(filter = "bayes|calibrated_thresholds")

They need ‘brms’ with a working Stan backend (‘rstan’ or ‘cmdstanr’ with CmdStan installed) and the suggested packages ‘posterior’ and ‘lme4’. They fit small models to the example data in system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog"); compilation dominates the run time, a few minutes on a laptop, and memory use is that of a normal Stan compilation. Run them before changing fit_calibration(), score_detections(), history_draws() or any other function that handles a brmsfit.

Life cycle

sheepdog is stable and actively maintained. Its version numbers follow semantic versioning: a change in the major version (as in 2.x to 3.0.0) may break existing code, and is documented in NEWS.md and, when it changes results, in a migration article such as vignette("migration-3.0.0"). Changes to defaults that alter results are announced with a warning before they take effect. Files written by earlier versions (clip manifests, validation tables and detection histories, back to the scripts of v1.2.0) remain readable. Planned work is tracked in the issues, including the alignment with the rOpenSci standards for statistical software.

Code style

  • Follow the tidyverse style guide and use the native pipe |>.
  • Exported functions use snake_case names in the object_verb or verb_object pattern already used in the package.
  • Talk to the user with message(), warning() and stop(), not with print() or cat(), except inside print() and format() methods.
  • Functions that write files take the output path or folder as an argument.

Code of conduct

Please note that this project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing, you agree to abide by its terms.
